summary: src/thumbnails.rs scales PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, ICO and TIFF files of up to 40 MB down itself on the three thumbnail threads (make_image: EXIF orientation, alpha-weighted averaging, the image crate's 512 MiB limit counted explicitly, a panicking decoder caught, the system's thumbnailer as the fallback) into the existing PNG cache in the data folder, keyed by path, date and thumbnail size. src/finder/views.rs (file_icon) sends raster images through that instead of img(path), which GPUI decoded whole and kept for good; SVG stays as it was; the thumbnail img has an ID, so its loading icon shows. src/finder/preview_images.rs (new) is a cache each browser has for the large previews: the last three images by path and date, pixels and textures freed on the way out, when the file changes and when the tab closes; src/finder/preview.rs draws the large image from it (gallery, column card, preview pane, Quick Look). Cargo.toml names the image crate's features (all built by GPUI already; Cargo.lock unchanged). In review: the thumbnail cache is now trimmed before the threads make thumbnails and not beside them, cached() takes the cache folder and has a test, one stale sentence of the manual is rewritten, and the commit message's changelog says what is still kept. Peak memory of the debug build drawn in software, measured again in review: icon view over 24 JPEGs of 3000x2000, 1924 MB before and 303-304 MB after (235 MB over an empty folder); gallery after each of the 24 was shown large, 2448 MB before and 570 MB after.
changelog: Browsing a folder of photos no longer fills memory. The icon view, the gallery strip, and Get Info loaded every PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, ICO, and TIFF image of up to 40 MB whole and kept it for as long as fffinder ran, about 48 MB for a 12-megapixel photo. They now show a thumbnail that fffinder scales down itself, the same on every system, and keeps with the system's thumbnails in the data folder. The large previews in the gallery, the column view, the preview pane, and Quick Look kept every image they loaded, and now keep the last three each tab or pane showed; a format the system draws, such as HEIC, is shown from its thumbnail as before. An image that was saved again now shows as it is once its folder is read again, as Refresh does, where it kept its old picture until fffinder was restarted. An item also shows its icon while its thumbnail is being made, where its place stayed empty, and an image that can't be read shows its icon with the extension badge.
behaviour_changes: Icon view, gallery strip, Get Info: a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, ICO or TIFF file of up to 40 MB shows a thumbnail fffinder scales down itself (64, 128, 256 or 512 px by icon size), no longer the whole file decoded and kept for the life of the app.

Those thumbnails are written as PNGs to thumbnails/ in the data folder (256 MB cap, trimmed when the first thumbnail of a session is asked for), as PDF and video thumbnails already were. So small copies of the photos you browse now stay on disk there, also of photos on volumes since removed. The manual's data-folder list says images are among them.

The first visit to a folder of photos fills in more slowly: three thumbnail threads decode, in the order asked, where all of GPUI's background threads did. Tiles scrolled past are still made before the ones in view. Later visits read the cache.
A tile shows its kind icon while its thumbnail is being made, from a fifth of a second into the wait, for PDFs, videos and documents too. Before, its place stayed empty.

An image that can't be decoded shows the document icon with its extension badge (was the plain image icon), after the system's thumbnailer has been tried too (it was not tried before; on macOS QuickLook may now draw a TIFF or ICO the image crate can't).

The first time the icon size asks for another thumbnail size (above 32, 64 or 128 points at the default UI scale), the image tiles in view are made again, each empty for a fifth of a second and then on its icon until its thumbnail is there. Before, the full image was simply rescaled.
A tile follows its file's date: an image saved again gets a new thumbnail once its folder is read again. Before, it kept its first picture until restart.

Large previews (gallery, column card, preview pane, Quick Look): each tab or pane keeps only the last three images it showed. Going back to an older one reads and decodes it again, its place empty meanwhile; before, it was instant and never freed. For a format GPUI can't decode (HEIC, RAW) that means the file is read whole again, to fail again, before the kept system thumbnail shows. Closing a tab frees its images.

A shown image whose file changed is read again when its row comes back with another date (folder read again, Refresh, a search run again). Nothing shows in its place while it is read, where other previews stay up until the new one is ready. Before, it was never read again. In the manual.
Refresh does not read an image again that was written over with its date kept, unlike other previews. Before, no image was read again at all. In the manual.
Thumbnails are box-averaged: fine detail looks smoother than the GPU's minification made it, and see-through edges are not darkened.

Edge cases: a file of up to 40 MB that decodes to more than 512 MiB (for a TIFF 256 MiB, by my reading of the image crate's limits, not run) gets the system's thumbnail or its icon in tiles, where GPUI drew it whole. A file with a raster extension that holds SVG text shows its icon in tiles (GPUI's loader fell back to SVG). Both still show large as before.
When the thumbnail cache can't be written (data folder read-only, disk full), image tiles keep their icons, where they used to show the image; PDFs and videos already did.

From review: the cache is trimmed by the thumbnail threads before the first thumbnail is made, no longer by a thread beside them. The first thumbnails of a session wait for the trim (a listing of the cache folder); no item is left on its icon because the trim removed the PNG being written or one just handed out.
Not user-visible: Finder::preview_images_for_test (doc-hidden) and thumbnails::IMAGE_LIMIT are new; thumbnails::cached takes the cache folder.
left_out: The spinner on the large image (the verifier dropped the proposal's step 4: it needs an ID on the large img, which would start GIF and WebP animations).
CHANGELOG.md (guide); the entry is in the commit message and here.
More thumbnail threads, newest-first order, cancelling tiles scrolled past (the plan's optional follow-up).
Freeing decoded tile thumbnails and SVG rasters (the plan leaves that retention, see notes).

Large previews that come from the system's thumbnail (HEIC, RAW, PSD; PDFs, videos and documents where their picture shows): the 1024-px thumbnail is still loaded through GPUI's own cache and kept for good, as before. See Found, not fixed.

Refresh reading an image again whatever its date says, and keeping the old picture up while a changed one is read: both settled in the manual instead (the implementer's deviations 10 and 11). I left them: the first would blank the shown image on every Refresh, the second needs a second load per entry.

Not tested: the icon shown while a thumbnail is made and the ID that makes it show (thumbnails are off under the test Recorder; pictured in /home/user/polish-tools/shots/thumbnail-memory-review-icons-loading.png); the fall back to the system's thumbnailer after a failed decode (it depends on what the machine has installed); that the trim comes before the first thumbnail (an order between threads).

Not run: clippy with --features term (nothing in src/term is touched and no signature it calls changed), and anything on macOS or Windows (the new code has no cfg of its own; only Linux compiles here).
review_fixes: The thumbnail cache was trimmed by a thread of its own beside the three that make thumbnails. Trimming removes every *.partial.png, which is what a thumbnail being written is (the rename then fails), and, over 256 MB, the PNGs used longest ago, which one a thread has just handed out can be (its date is marked after the trim read it). Either left that item on its icon until restart. It was there for PDFs and videos (the implementer found it and left it as not his); with every photo of the first folder going through the queue while the trim runs, this change made it far more likely, so it is closed here: the three threads go through a std::sync::Once that trims before any of them takes a job. No test: it is an order between threads.

What makes an image thumbnail happen, cached() choosing make_image over the system's thumbnailer and putting the PNG in the cache, had no test: the UI tests can't see thumbnails and the unit tests called make_image directly. cached() now takes the cache folder (it wrote to the real data folder), and an_image_is_scaled_down_into_the_cache_and_read_from_it_after pins the path, the size, that nothing unfinished is left, and that the image isn't read a second time. With the in-process branch taken out it fails here (no thumbnailer installed).

docs/manual.md, the line under the list of views: "Thumbnails cover PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, ICO, TIFF, and SVG files up to 40 MB, and on macOS PDFs, videos, and documents" was wrong before this change about macOS and is wrong after it about 40 MB (larger images get the system's thumbnail). It now reads "Thumbnails cover images, PDFs, videos, and documents, on every system", with the details left to the Thumbnails section it points to.

Commit message. The changelog entry said the icon view loaded "every" such image whole (only those of up to 40 MB), and that the large previews keep only the last three images, without the exception that matters most on a Mac: a HEIC (or RAW) photo is shown large from the system's 1024-px thumbnail, which is kept as before. Both are said now, in the body too. The figures are the ones measured again in review, with the gallery's before (2448 MB), which was missing.

No other change to the source. I broke each rule of the image cache in turn (no eviction, no texture drop, the changed file kept beside the new, no date in the key, no release with the tab, no move to the back) and each time a test failed; reverse-applying views.rs and preview.rs fails all five UI tests.
notes:
Checked. All five UI tests fail with src/finder/views.rs and src/finder/preview.rs reverse-applied (the test accessor kept, or tests/controls.rs would not compile), and six mutations of preview_images.rs each fail one or two of them. I read every changed function whole and GPUI's side of each call (img.rs, image_cache.rs, asset_cache.rs, window.rs drop_image, platform.rs decode_static_image), the image crate's reader, limits and set_limits of each decoder, and taffy's leaf layout. The implementer's claims held: GPUI's loader does not count the decoded picture against the limit after into_decoder and ImageReader::decode does; an orientation that can't be read fails GPUI's decode too, so `.ok()?` loses nothing; the image crate is built once with GPUI's features, so both decode the same files; QuickLook is asked for a thumbnail only, never an icon, so a broken image falls back to fffinder's icon on macOS too. Pictures taken with the reviewed build (thumbnail-memory-review-*.png): every format has its thumbnail, the EXIF-turned photos are upright in the tiles and in the large preview (the strip and Get Info draw the same thumbnails; Get Info is pictured with portrait.jpg, inside its box), the loading picture has the JPG icon on the one tile still being made. Memory measured again, before and after (figures in summary). check.sh printed CHECK OK on the commit as it went onto the trunk, rebased over e2e1672 and ac62eaf (805 passed in 16 test binaries, 3/3 known root-only failures). The run before the rebase passed every test (785) and stopped on a clippy lint in the test added in review, which was fixed before that. The two trunk commits the rebase brought in touch views.rs (a middle press on a folder), mod.rs (a count for the status bar), the manual and tests/controls.rs elsewhere: nothing this change reads or writes.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt, each held against the code.
1. A photo's thumbnail that never comes, or comes wrong, where the photo itself used to show. Same decoders as GPUI and the format taken from the content first; orientation, alpha, 16 bits, CMYK, animations (first frame, as before) are in the tests and the 22-encodings picture; the trim can no longer take a thumbnail away (fixed in review); a decoder panic is caught. What remains: if the cache folder can't be written, images show icons.
2. The window feeling slower. Nothing new runs on the window's thread (the job is sent on an unbounded channel; the cache holds three entries). But the first fill is on three threads in the order asked, with no cancelling, and a change of icon size across 32, 64 or 128 points makes the tiles in view again.
3. A texture freed while it is on screen, or memory that still grows. One browser shows at most two different images at a time (its window and Quick Look both draw the primary entry; the gallery's first-item fallback only when nothing is selected), all from the same rows, so with three kept the one let go of is never one being drawn; textures are dropped in every window. What still grows is listed below.

Doubts that remain.
1. Only Linux was built and run. The owner uses macOS: there, a HEIC or RAW photo is shown large from QuickLook's 1024-px thumbnail, kept as before, so the gallery over a folder of iPhone originals still gains about 3 MB of pixels and as much texture per photo shown. The changelog entry says so; the icon view over such a folder never loaded them whole.
2. Tile thumbnails are never freed (the plan's choice): 44 KB of pixels and as much texture per photo at the default icon size, up to 1 MB at the largest. Tens of thousands of photos scrolled through in one session still come to gigabytes. The disk cache is trimmed only once a session, so it can pass 256 MB until the next start.
3. An SVG tile is still drawn by GPUI at the size the file declares (capped at 8192 px a side) and kept: an illustration with a 4000x3000 canvas costs 48 MB for good, like a photo did. The brief kept SVG "because it is small", which is true of icons and not of exported artwork.
4. FIFO on three threads, no cancellation: after a fast scroll through a large unvisited folder the tiles in view wait behind every tile passed.
5. Each icon-size class is a separate thumbnail (2 px per point): crossing 32, 64 or 128 points blanks the image tiles in view until they are made again, once per folder and class, and on a display scaled above 200% thumbnails are scaled up.
6. Nothing shows while a changed image is read again, and Refresh does not read an image again whose date was kept (deviations 10 and 11, both in the manual). The key could take the entry's size too, as the other previews' stamp does; I left it as the plan has it.
7. A thumbnail made while its file was still being written is kept under the date the row had then; it is replaced when the row comes back with another date, which a file written in place only does once its folder changes again or on Refresh (that part is as stale-previews-and-cancel left it).
8. The implementer saw one run of the screenshot example over an EMPTY folder peak at 1499 MB and never again in 59 runs. I ran it once: 235 MB. Unexplained, and nothing of this change runs there.

For the changelog: stale-previews-and-cancel's entry ends "and a picture still shows as it was first drawn until fffinder is restarted". This change makes that untrue; its done record asks for the clause to go when the changelog is assembled.

Briefs still to come.

Its verifier's second reason against the clamp (the icon view and the strip load the same img(path) asset) no longer holds: tiles show shrunk copies, and only SVG tiles load the file. The decoded image is in the browser's cache once loaded (preview_images.rs `held()`, `RenderImage::size(0)` is the upright pixel size), but a header read on the preview thread is still the simpler source of the dimensions. Cargo.toml now names the image crate's bmp, gif, ico, jpeg, png, tiff and webp features.
preview-card-height, quick-look-empty-state, preview-page-keys, table-preview-column-widths: no arm in common; the image arm's layout is untouched, only its source changed.
icon-tile-hit-target, inactive-selection-colour, multi-word-highlights, view-switch-keeps-selection, select-all-perf: render_tile and render_strip_tile are untouched. In file_icon the thumbnail `img` has the ID ("thumbnail", path_id) and `thumbnailable` became `draws_itself` (SVG only). If icon-tile-hit-target rebuilds the tile, see the first item of Found, not fixed: the icon's box is where the fix goes.
get-info-stop-walk: src/finder/info.rs is untouched; its icon is a thumbnail now, keyed by the date `FileEntry::from_path` reads at each render (see Found, not fixed, 4).
fix-wording-after-later-changes and the final changelog: the clause above. The manual's Images row and the paragraph under the preview table were rewritten here; the line under the list of views too.

Found, not fixed (all on the trunk before this change).
1. Icon view and gallery strip: an image taller than wide is drawn at the icon's width and its own proportions, so a portrait photo runs over its name and a very tall one (a long screenshot) over the rows below, to the bottom of the view. See portrait.jpg and phone photo.jpg in thumbnail-memory-before-icons-light.png and thumbnail-memory-review-icons-light.png, and "19 tall.png" in thumbnail-memory-after-many-encodings-light.png. Cause, read and not run: GPUI's Img sets the style's aspect_ratio from the image when none is set (img.rs request_layout), and taffy's leaf layout gives a block-level leaf height = max(height, width / aspect_ratio); the tile's icon is such a leaf (its wrapper is a plain div). Get Info, where the icon is a flex item, is right. Candidate fix, not tried: `.aspect_square()` on the two imgs in file_icon; object_fit(Contain) then letterboxes inside the square from the image's own size. It needs a test, and under the test Recorder thumbnails don't load, so the test would go through an SVG file, whose img has no ID to measure. Most phone photos are portrait: worth the owner's eye.
2. The large previews keep the system's 1024-px thumbnail of everything shown through it (HEIC, RAW, PSD; PDFs until hayro has drawn, videos, documents) for good, up to 4 MB of pixels and as much texture each: large_thumbnail loads it with thumbnails::image through GPUI's app-wide asset cache, which nothing empties. A second deque in PreviewImages for these, beside the one for originals (a failed original takes a slot of its own, so one deque of three would thrash), would bound it.
3. SVG tiles (doubt 3 above): drawing an SVG's thumbnail with resvg at the tile's size would need GPUI's font setup to keep text looking the same.
4. src/finder/info.rs single_item calls FileEntry::from_path at every render of Get Info: a stat on the window's thread per frame.
5. A search hit whose index entry has no date (modified 0) gives its thumbnail the date 0, so it is not made again when the file changes while it is listed that way. As it was for PDFs; I did not look for when the index has no date.
6. Not faults of fffinder, for whoever compares pictures: the image crate refuses an ICO whose PNG entries are RGB (Pillow writes them from an RGB image; app.ico in the pictures), and reads a 32-bit BMP's fourth byte as padding where Pillow wrote alpha (15 alpha.bmp shows black). GPUI drew both the same way before.
